frictionTaskLines.text: review found 2 defects — the 1.0.0 guard read package.json instead of the tag-derived old_version (wrong after a partial release), and the `**/.mise/` pathspec silently matches nothing under default git pathspec magic

the defect was seeded by the plan's own wording — step 9 and its checklist said the guard reads "the current version", which reads as package.json; the tag-derived old_version is what the computation actually uses. Plan prose that names a value imprecisely propagates straight into code.
review found MAINTAINERS.md recommending npm classic tokens, which npm disabled 2025-11-05 and revoked 2025-12-09 — stale-world knowledge in a doc the maintainer executes cold at a hard stop

dependabot activated on repo creation and merged a firebase-tools bump within two minutes, moving main and invalidating the exact version string task 1.3 recorded for task 2.4 to reuse — plan-time constants about mutable dependency state go stale between tasks

Yarn 4's `run` global-script fallback (any script name containing a colon resolves to the single workspace defining it, from any workspace) caused infinite recursion with `test:unit` and triple-execution with `ci:test-emulator`; the plan's test-orchestration design assumed colon names were free. Per-package scripts must be colon-free.

review found 3 public-API breaks introduced to satisfy a lint rule (ActionableFunctionCallerOptions gained a required first type param; TMap constraint narrowed to RequestResponseMap<TCommand>; failEntriesWith narrowed unknown->Error). The implementer framed it as a two-way choice; the reviewer built and verified a third option that satisfies the rule with zero API change. Lint-driven edits to exp

review found 4 defects — a weakened test (async dropped instead of returning a promise, collapsing a case into its neighbour), ./mocks published types narrowed where 2 of 3 files had no lint pressure at all (119 of the 121 findings were in EXCLUDED test files), a silent runtime error-wrapping change in setEnqueueFailure that step 9 said to raise rather than resolve, and three symbols newly exporte

review found 5 prose defects that type-checking cannot catch — chiefly a false compile-time guarantee ("a write placed before a read cannot compile"; the wrappers are handed to the callback simultaneously, so it compiles and fails at runtime). Self-verifying examples by compiling them proves syntax, not semantics.

frictionOtherLines: requirements: goals bootstrap phase 1 ("push to main") is unexecutable under the repo's own `.mise/` guard and the CLAUDE.md never-merge rule — the contradiction survived the goals gate

requirements: goals fixed placeholder version at `0.0.1` while also requiring the first real release be `1.0.0`; conventional-changelog cannot bridge those, so an approved goal was mechanically impossible

requirements: goals recorded scdate as the template for dependabot auto-merge and for provenance without checking what scdate actually does — scdate auto-merges npm majors and has no provenance at all

goals: two dependency-metadata decisions were taken with the maintainer during the requirements stage and left unrecorded in goals.md for a round, so the two approved documents contradicted each other on their face

plan critic: round 1 disproved the versioning mechanism recorded in approved goals decision 8 — with skip-commit true the changelog action reads git TAGS, not package.json, so the 0.0.1 placeholder was never consulted and the first release would have computed 0.1.0; three earlier requirements rounds verified bumpVersion.js without ever checking which strategy feeds it
plan critic: round 1 also found the prescribed phase-1 root tsconfig cannot compile at all (TS18002 on an empty files list with empty references), so task 1.1 could not have ended green

attw audit (out-of-plan): the packages shipped 56 undeclared module references in published .d.ts, of which only 29 ever produced an error — the other 27 sat in lazily-checked nested type positions. arethetypeswrong was clean on all three and did NOT catch it, because it resolves entry points without typechecking .d.ts bodies. Neither the plan nor any critic round anticipated declaration-emit spec
